items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: I remember the first time that I really improvised with someone else. It was a guitarist named Baird Hersey came over to my place

ctx.x: Two compliments. So you came from — into this field as a classical player, is that correct?

Originally, originally yes. But most of the time I was playing classical music I was also improvising for modern dance classes and I did that as a job for years. So that was — yeah I had some experience in improvising but it was a different kind of thing, you know there were boundaries to it, you are playing for this exercise and I would often do a repetitive kind of thing. And I remember the first time that I really improvised with someone else. It was a guitarist named Baird Hersey came over to my place and he…

To be terrified there has to be, in my opinion, a fear of doing something wrong. So what constitutes wrongness at that — do you recall what would have made it sound wrong to you? Were you playing chordally?
